title: A Songbook for the Letters
premise: Orsen Almeida has built a career on other people's voices, ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrated violinist Ivo Marchetti while nursing an old, unspoken love for her college friend Teodor Lindqvist. When a letter Teodor mailed to her eleven years ago — lost in a dead-letter office — finally surfaces, Orsen must decide whether to read the confession inside or keep hiding behind the sentences she writes for others. As she drafts Ivo's memoir, she discovers Ivo's own buried history of stolen credit and a silenced protégée, forcing Orsen to choose between professional loyalty and justice no court will deliver. In the end she reads the letter aloud to Teodor at last, says her rehearsed sentence back to him, and exposes Ivo's theft in the memoir's final pages — finding belonging not in a finished book, but in a voice that is finally, unmistakably her own.
about_author: Beatrix Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing undelivered letters before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town in Maine, where she keeps a drawer of postcards addressed to people she can no longer find.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Obeys
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She finishes a chapter of Ivo Marchetti's memoir in Ivo's voice, then declines — again — Teodor's invitation to dinner, telling herself the heart is trainable. Establishes her doctrine of containment and the ache beneath it. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for discipline.

chapters.title: Dead Letter Office
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A postal clerk calls: an eleven-year-old letter, water-stained but legible, postmarked the night everything between Orsen and Teodor went silent. She signs for it and does not open it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity; the past arrives with a tracking number.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with flashback. The night of the letter: a graduation recital, a misunderstanding involving Teodor's brother, and the sentence Orsen never said. We learn why she vanished into ghostwriting. Emotional beat: grief reframed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Ivo's Voice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At Ivo's lakeside estate, Orsen interviews her about the legendary year Ivo 'discovered' her signature piece. Ivo is magnetic, evasive, controlling. Teodor appears — he's the estate's luthier, repairing Ivo's violins. First collision in a decade. Emotional beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. He recognized Orsen's cadence in Ivo's published acknowledgments years ago and never said so. Repairing a violin whose varnish hides another maker's label, he thinks about hidden authorship. He asks Orsen to stay for the restoration. Emotional beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Unopened
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Alone at night, she holds the letter over a candle flame as if to destroy it unread, then can't. She locks it in her manuscript case beside Ivo's chapters. Emotional beat: the cost of a sentence unsaid compounding interest for a decade.

chapters.title: The Protégée
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Researching Ivo's early career, Orsen finds a name scrubbed from every program: Ana Reyes, a violinist who vanished after co-writing what became Ivo's signature piece. A librarian sends one surviving cassette of Ana playing. Emotional beat: the ghostwriter recognizes a ghosted woman.

chapters.title: Duet, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. Working late in the workshop, he and Orsen play the cassette and fall into easy rhythm — tea, jokes, old shorthand returning. Almost-touch moment interrupted by Ivo summoning Orsen for revisions. Emotional beat: warmth with a timer on it.

chapters.title: Revisions
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ivo demands the memoir portray Ana as a 'brief, unremarkable student.' Orsen complies, hating herself, and realizes she is doing to Ana exactly what the world did to her own voice. Emotional beat: complicity as self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Ana's Address
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Tracking Ana to a small-town music school in Ohio, Orsen calls her. Ana is guarded, then furious, then quietly devastating: she stopped playing because the world believed Ivo. She agrees to talk only if Orsen comes in person. Emotional beat: righteous anger as invitation.

chapters.title: The Road Out of the Book
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. He drives Orsen to Ohio without asking why; the road trip reopens their old intimacy, including the almost-said things from eleven years ago. He tells her about the letter he mailed that night — and that she never answered. Orsen goes silent. Emotional beat: two people discovering they were both waiting.

chapters.title: Cassette Evidence
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In Ana's kitchen, Ana plays rehearsal tapes showing the piece was composed jointly, dated before Ivo's claim, plus a contract Ivo had her sign and later voided. Orsen records everything, knowing it could end her career. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What Justice Isn't
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Back at the estate, Orsen weighs options: lawyers won't touch a stale claim; exposure means Ivo torches her reputation first. She drafts a confession chapter in Ivo's voice as a test — and realizes she can write Ivo admitting anything. Power and nausea arrive together. Emotional beat: the ethics of ventriloquism.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV (first time). Ivo suspects Orsen knows about Ana; she probes with charm and veiled threats, revealing she once received — and burned — a copy of a letter Teodor wrote, believing she was protecting everyone. Emotional beat: villainy with wounds; the reader learns the letter's loss wasn't accident alone.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts Teodor: why did he stop writing after one letter? He shows her his draft replies, dozens, all unsent — he thought her silence was the answer. They circle the truth like musicians afraid of the downbeat. Emotional beat: mutual misreading laid bare, still unresolved.

chapters.title: Premiere
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ivo's memoir launches with a gala concert featuring the disputed piece. Ana attends uninvited. Mid-performance, Ivo dedicates the work to 'my own hand alone' — and Orsen, in the audience, decides. Emotional beat: public lie as trigger; the room becomes a courtroom.

chapters.title: Read It Aloud
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Backstage, Orsen gives Ivo a choice: publish the true acknowledgment chapter Orsen wrote, or Orsen releases the tapes and walks. Ivo threatens ruin; Orsen answers by saying, aloud, the sentence she rehearsed for eleven years — not to Ivo, but to Teodor standing in the doorway. Emotional beat: climax; the private sentence detonates in a public war.

chapters.title: Fallout in F Sharp
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. The acknowledgment chapter leaks; press descends; Ivo sues Orsen for breach. Teodor stands beside her publicly, costing him the estate workshop and Ivo's patronage network. Emotional beat: love proven by shared loss rather than declaration.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Rather than a court, Orsen brokers justice outside the law: Ivo publicly credits Ana, funds a scholarship in her name, and withdraws the suit — in exchange for the tapes staying sealed. Ana gets her name on the score; Orsen gets no credit at all, and finds she doesn't need it. Emotional beat: bittersweet, principled peace.

chapters.title: Return to Sender, Finally Opened
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With everything settled, Orsen finally opens the eleven-year-old letter. It says only: 'Ask me the question you already know. I'll wait as long as it takes.' She laughs until she cries — the answer was always hers to give. Emotional beat: release; the letter was a mirror, not a verdict.

chapters.title: A Songbook for the Letters
chapters.summary: Alternating Orsen/Teodor POV. Teodor finishes restoring the violin with Ana's hidden label restored beneath fresh varnish; Ana plays it at the scholarship's first recital. Orsen begins writing under her own name — a novel about a dead-letter office. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, authored, signed.

chapters.title: Coda: Postmarked Today
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, brief and lyrical. One year later: Orsen mails Teodor a letter of her own, though he's asleep upstairs — a habit of honesty now, not distance. The final line is the sentence from chapter 17, written this time in her hand. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the heart, trained at last toward openness.
